cells.tense: The pen is in your hand right now and you know the next line.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are steering on purpose, out loud, to someone who will just listen — and let their not answering be fine.
cells.core:
The ground is clearing under you and you are choosing from the clearing, not the panic. Something that couldn't hold has already given way, and instead of scrambling for the shape it used to have, you're pointing attention where you mean it to go. This is not force. It's picking, plainly, and meaning it.

You say what you want without needing the picture whole. You keep the direction after the first bright feeling fades, holding the line without gripping it. Nothing here needs certainty from you, only one thing picked and stayed with past the quiet. The rest can settle at its own speed while you work.
cells.sheetLine: You pick the direction, and you keep picking it.

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future you keep trying to write in advance.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you want settled by next week and leave it alone until someone brings it to you; let what you want stand without being pushed.
cells.core:
You're trying to get the clearing to finish on your schedule. The pressure is on how fast people catch up, how soon this resolves, what it looks like when it's done — and you're managing all of it ahead of time. That racing feeling is not direction. It's grip.

Seeing the whole pattern, all layers at once, and still letting it stay open is the free version of this. The clarity that got you here is exactly what the pushing costs you. What is actually clear can stand a week with no hand on it. Set it down and find out what it looks like without you steering.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you some time before now.
cells.ask: Take one visible step toward something you want, whether the last one worked or not, knowing it might not land either.
cells.core:
The clearing happened and you didn't walk through. Something used to hold here and it broke, and you took that as the answer about what happens when you try. So now the question comes before the act — what's the point. That is the part that isn't moving.

Wanting something on purpose and moving toward it without proof it will hold is the free version. You can choose a direction before the ground is certain under it. What you are doesn't need proving before it takes a step. Move before the ache of the last one clears, and let that step be small.

cells.tense: The pen is down but the writing you do hasn't stopped.
cells.ask: Say 'I chose this' about one thing today you'd normally call obvious or just how it happened, and let it be strange to say.
cells.core:
You're steering and calling it drift. Things around here got cleared out and rearranged while you described it as circumstances settling, or as just following what was there. The direction keeps going. The owning of it doesn't.

Claiming what you're already moving toward, without turning it into a performance, is the free version of this. You can start smaller than you think. Nothing rides on the size of the admission, only on saying it plainly once. Notice one thing you decided today and filed under how it happens, and name yourself as the one who picked it.
